concepts.def: IBDP Music 2020 syllabus organises study around four areas: music for sociocultural and political expression, for listening and performance, for dramatic impact, presentation, entertainment.
Personal or community traditions students draw on; required as first lens for global comparison in the exploring component.
Coursework requires study of at least four musical contexts; cannot be from same geographical/cultural cluster.
Bruno Nettl's Study of Ethnomusicology 1983 framed music in cultural context as central; Nettl identified 29 issues for the field.
Cross-cultural exchange spans Silk Road via Marco Polo (1271-95), West African to Caribbean (transatlantic), Beatles to Indian classical (1965 Norwegian Wood).
Coined 1987 at London meeting of independent labels (Globestyle, Cooking Vinyl); marketing category for non-Western traditions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Exploring Music in Context — a core area of Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exploring Music in Context brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exploring Music in Context.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In what year was the world music label adopted by indie labels?
How many musical contexts minimum must IBDP exploring cover?
What does the time signature 6/8 indicate?
options: A piece six bars long.
Music in 3/4 time.
Six beats per bar, all equal in stress.
Two beats per bar, each beat divided into three (compound duple).

mcqs.q: What does 'piano' (p) mean as a dynamic marking?
options: Quiet/soft.
Slow.
The instrument piano.
Music in 3/4 time.
Slow.
Three sections: A, contrasting B, and a return to A (ABA).
Three different sections (ABC).
Music in 3/4 time.
